research_question: When six frozen learned views are progressively merged into fewer registered components, does PACT's analytic evidence-budget order determine its empirical selective-decision order?
scope: PACT-specific exhaustive coarsening analysis over frozen HandWritten-Mfeat TMC and RCML per-view evidence. It evaluates every set partition of six observed views and every one-step merge relation. It does not test false splitting, learn a provenance partition, or compare registration-blind operators across the 203 partitions.

partition_space.edge_direction: fine-to-coarse by merging exactly two registered components
partition_space.declared_policy: six singleton acquisition views; this is the unique finest partition and its rank is therefore not an empirical estimand

primary_estimand.name: cover-edge selective-order transfer
primary_estimand.definition: For each of the 856 fixed fine-to-coarse cover edges, compute delta ncsAURC = ncsAURC(coarse) - ncsAURC(fine). Report the fractions for which coarsening improves, worsens, or ties selective risk.
primary_estimand.falsifiable_reference: Universal transfer of the analytic budget order to selective risk permits no cover edge on which coarsening improves ncsAURC.
primary_estimand.interpretation: A nonzero coarsening-improves fraction shows that evidence-budget monotonicity alone does not fix the empirical selective ordering on these frozen outputs; it is not a general sufficiency theorem.

secondary_estimands: Within each component count k, IQR, range, and median absolute deviation of ncsAURC across partitions, quantifying composition dependence beyond component count.
Accuracy, mean evidence budget, and posterior L1 displacement from the six-singleton partition for every partition.
Score-tie diagnostics for every partition and frozen emitter realization.

scores.reporting_rule: Both score analyses are reported regardless of direction; no score is selected from test outcomes.

selective_metric.name: continuous tie-aware normalized common-support area under the risk-coverage curve
selective_metric.support_rule: Fixed before outcome inspection and shared by every partition and pair; no partition may shrink the evaluation support.
selective_metric.tie_rule: Analytic fractional inclusion within each equal-score group.
selective_metric.integration: Closed-form continuous integral over the fixed coverage interval rather than an arbitrary record ordering within ties.

bootstrap.pairing: All five frozen emitter realizations, all 203 partitions, all 856 cover edges, and both predeclared scores attached to each sampled record are carried together.
bootstrap.aggregation: Compute each partition metric within emitter realization, then average the five frozen realizations. Do not treat realizations as independent observations.
bootstrap.interpretation: Intervals are conditional on the five frozen emitter realizations.

required: The directed one-merge cover graph contains 856 edges.
For every record, emitter realization, and cover edge, coarse evidence budget does not exceed fine evidence budget.
Both HandWritten-Mfeat pairs contain exactly five frozen emitter realizations and the locked record denominators.
integrity_gates.failure_action: Stop outcome reporting and emit the failed gate.

reporting_constraints: Report TMC and RCML separately; do not pool their outcomes.
Do not report a declared-partition rank because the six-singleton policy is constructively the finest partition.
Do not interpret the 203-partition surface as a false-splitting test; false splitting remains the separate registered-copy intervention.
Do not tune registration, scores, support, or reporting direction from test labels.
Report results even if the declared accounting policy is not outcome-optimal.
Describe the structural budget check as implementation consistency, not empirical proof of the analytic corollary.
